selected.name: Data at Rest Encryption
selected.rationale: customer PII (names, emails, passwords, task data) stored on managed cloud → GDPR Art. 32 security of processing (encryption at rest)

selected.name: Data in Transit Encryption
selected.rationale: PII transmitted via SaaS web/mobile interface and payment-provider API → GDPR Art. 32 security of processing (encryption in transit)

selected.name: Vulnerability Identification
selected.rationale: TinyTask develops and places SaaS product on EU market as manufacturer → CRA Art. 13(1) vulnerability identification

selected.name: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
selected.rationale: TinyTask places product with digital elements on EU market as manufacturer → CRA Art. 13(1) coordinated vulnerability disclosure

selected.name: Identity Lifecycle Management
selected.rationale: customer accounts with individual logins for business customers and their end-users → GDPR Art. 32 identity lifecycle management

selected.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
selected.rationale: individual login accounts with stored passwords → GDPR Art. 32 authentication strength

selected.name: Incident Detection & Triage
selected.rationale: processing of PII (names, emails, passwords, task data) on managed cloud → GDPR Art. 33 breach detection and triage

selected.name: Incident Notification & Reporting
selected.rationale: personal data breach involving customer PII → GDPR Art. 33(1) 72-hour notification to supervisory authority

selected.name: Data Minimisation
selected.rationale: collection of customer names, emails, passwords, and task data → GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation

selected.name: Retention & Archiving
selected.rationale: storage of customer PII and task data on managed cloud → GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation

selected.name: Right to Erasure
selected.rationale: customer and end-user PII stored in SaaS → GDPR Art. 17 right to erasure

selected.name: Data Portability
selected.rationale: customer PII (names, emails, task data) held in structured format → GDPR Art. 20 data portability

selected.name: Vendor Risk Assessment
selected.rationale: external payment provider as sub-processor + managed cloud hosting → GDPR Art. 28 processor due diligence

selected.name: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
selected.rationale: TinyTask develops SaaS product and places on EU market as manufacturer → CRA Art. 13(1) SBOM

selected.name: Contractual Security Obligations
selected.rationale: external payment provider and managed cloud as processors → GDPR Art. 28(3) contractual security obligations

selected.name: Secure-by-Design Principles
selected.rationale: TinyTask develops SaaS product from scratch → GDPR Art. 25 data protection by design + CRA security by design

selected.name: Secure Coding Practices
selected.rationale: in-house development of SaaS product with digital elements → CRA secure coding practices

selected.name: Information Security Policies
selected.rationale: 8-person SaaS company processing PII → GDPR Art. 32 documented security measures

selected.name: Impact & Risk Assessments
selected.rationale: processing of PII (names, emails, passwords, task data) → GDPR Art. 35 risk assessment

selected.name: Records of Processing
selected.rationale: controller and processor roles for PII → GDPR Art. 30 records of processing activities

selected.name: Continuous Security Monitoring
selected.rationale: SaaS product processing PII on managed cloud → GDPR Art. 32 continuous security monitoring

selected.name: Audit Logging & Traceability
selected.rationale: processing of PII with individual logins → GDPR Art. 32 audit logging and traceability

excluded.why: key custody separation is a sub-component of D-01.1/D-01.2; managed cloud provider handles key management; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
data integrity is implied by D-01.1/D-01.2 encryption controls; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
patch management is a sub-component of D-02.1 vulnerability identification; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
"threat-led" and TLPT are disproportionate for 8-person company with self-assessment conformity; basic security testing is covered by D-02.1
least privilege is a sub-component of D-03.1/D-03.2 identity management; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
secure defaults are a sub-component of D-07.1 secure by design; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
incident containment is a sub-component of D-04.1 incident detection; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
incident recovery is a sub-component of D-04.1 incident detection; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
third-party boundary management is a sub-component of D-06.1/D-06.3 vendor risk; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
CI/CD pipeline security is a sub-component of D-07.1/D-07.2 secure development; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
change management is a sub-component of D-07.1 secure by design; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
general security awareness is a generic obligation not clearly triggered by a specific company fact
role-specific competence is a generic obligation not clearly triggered by a specific company fact
subject matter targets NIS2 essential/important entities and DORA financial entities; neither applies to TinyTask
asset inventory is a sub-component of D-09.1 security policies; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
compliance testing is a sub-component of D-02.1/D-07.1; no distinct company fact triggers it independently
